answer: I'd like to talk about a problem at work that had nothing to do with paperwork and everything to do with people. A difficult problem I once solved involved a serious misunderstanding between two members of a team I was working with at the consultancy. One of them handled students' documents and the other handled visa files, and each felt the other was causing delays. Their disagreement had escalated to the point where it was affecting everyone's work. At first I was reluctant to get involved, because it was not really my responsibility, but I could see the whole office was suffering. Rather than taking sides, I decided to sit down with each of them separately to understand their perspectives. It quickly became clear that the whole conflict stemmed from poor communication rather than any real [[malice]]. I then arranged a calm conversation between them over tea, acting as a neutral [[mediator]]. It was a delicate situation that required a lot of [[tact]], but eventually they [[cleared the air]]. We also agreed on a simple shared checklist, so nobody would be left guessing about who was doing what. What I found most rewarding was seeing them work together productively again afterwards. Honestly, resolving that tension felt like a genuine achievement, and it taught me the value of listening carefully before [[jumping to conclusions]]. It made me realise that many difficult problems are really just communication failures in disguise, and patience is often the best tool. I still feel quite proud of how that turned out.

followUps.q: Do the two colleagues get on well now?
followUps.answer: Surprisingly well, yes. They still tease each other now and then, but it is friendly. They even sit together at lunch, which nobody in the office would have predicted a year ago.

followUps.q: Do you enjoy solving problems like this?
followUps.answer: I do, as long as they don't happen too often. I find it satisfying to untangle a situation and see people relax again, although it can be quite draining while it is going on.

note: Set at his consultancy with documents vs visa roles; added the shared checklist; plain mark 'communication' replaced by 'cleared the air' and 'jumping to conclusions'.
